about_blocks.text: London Trauma Therapy is a private outpatient psychotherapy practice in London, Ontario. It is not a residential rehab. People come in for 50-minute sessions at the office on Wellington Road in south London or the smaller office in Komoka, or they meet their therapist online from anywhere in the province. There are no beds and no medical detox.

People come in for 50-minute sessions at the office on Wellington Road in south London or the smaller office in Komoka, or they meet their therapist online from anywhere in the province. about_blocks.text: Trauma is the main focus. The practice was founded by Jordan Thomas, MSW, who says on its website that she started it after recovering from PTSD herself. Its therapists work with childhood sexual abuse, sexual and physical violence, car accidents, attachment trauma, PTSD and complex trauma, using EMDR, Cognitive Processing Therapy, DBT, CBT, Internal Family Systems and somatic therapy.

about_blocks.text: Addiction comes up here mostly where it overlaps with trauma and mental health. Addiction and recovery is one of the practice's listed specialties, and its therapy pages describe substance use work that looks at what sits underneath the drinking or drug use. That makes it a reasonable choice for someone whose substance use is tied to old trauma, anxiety or depression, or for outpatient support after a residential program ends.

about_blocks.text: The team has more than 25 registered social workers and registered psychotherapists, all registered with the OCSWSSW or the CRPO. They see adults, teens, children, couples and families, and the practice runs a separate service for first responders, veterans and healthcare workers. A Client Care Team matches each new client with a therapist rather than handing out whoever is free.

centre.faq_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About London Trauma Therapy

faqs.question: Is London Trauma Therapy a residential rehab?

answer_blocks.text: No. London Trauma Therapy is an outpatient psychotherapy practice, so you book 50-minute sessions and go home afterwards. It has no beds, no overnight stays and no medical detox. Sessions happen at its offices in south London and Komoka, or online anywhere in Ontario. If you need live-in addiction treatment or supervised withdrawal, look at residential centres in Ontario first and use therapy here alongside or after that care.

faqs.question: Does London Trauma Therapy help with addiction and substance use?

answer_blocks.text: Yes, as part of outpatient counselling. The practice lists addiction and recovery among the issues its therapists work with, and its therapy pages describe substance use work that looks at the problems underneath the drinking or drug use and builds other ways of coping. Several therapists, including Gordana Cvetkovic, name addiction as an area they support. It does not prescribe medication or run a detox or structured rehab program.

faqs.question: How much does therapy cost, and is it covered by benefits?

answer_blocks.text: Sessions cost $150 to $180 for 50 minutes, according to the practice's fees page. OHIP does not cover them, but many workplace extended health plans and EAPs cover sessions with registered social workers and registered psychotherapists. Psychotherapist fees have HST added; social workers do not charge HST. The practice bills the Canadian Armed Forces, NIHB and Victim Services directly, and fees are paid by debit or credit at each session.

faqs.question: What kinds of trauma do the therapists treat?

answer_blocks.text: The trauma team works with childhood sexual abuse, incest, sexual violence, physical violence, car accidents and attachment trauma, along with PTSD and complex trauma. Therapists use EMDR, Cognitive Processing Therapy, DBT, CBT, Internal Family Systems and somatic therapy, and the approach is chosen with you at the first appointment. There is also a dedicated service for first responders, veterans and healthcare workers.

faqs.question: Is there a waitlist, and do I need a referral?

answer_blocks.text: There is no waitlist and you do not need a referral. The practice says it can often book same-week appointments, and sometimes same-day ones. You can book online through its Jane booking site, call 226-777-7702, or email the Client Care Team, who will suggest a therapist who suits what you need.

faqs.question: Can I try a therapist before committing?

answer_blocks.text: Yes. You can book a free 15-minute consultation call with a therapist to see whether their style suits you, and the practice suggests trying two or three at most. It also offers a match guarantee: if your therapist turns out not to be a good fit, Client Care moves you to another one and that first session is free.

faqs.question: Where are the offices, and how do I get there?

answer_blocks.text: The main office is at 743 Wellington Road, Unit 4, in south London, close to Highway 401, Victoria Hospital and White Oaks Mall. Park for free at the back of the building and take the stairs on the far right, next to Hakim Optical. The second office is at 9918 Glendon Drive, Unit 4, in Komoka, about 20 minutes west, with free parking out front. From Toronto, London is roughly two hours by car along the 401.

faqs.question: Does London Trauma Therapy see children, teens, couples and families?

answer_blocks.text: Yes. The practice offers individual therapy for adults, child and youth therapy, teen therapy, couples counselling and family therapy. Age ranges depend on the therapist; some see children from age 6 and others start at 13 or 14. A parent or guardian has to consent for anyone under 18, and some therapists also provide Voice of the Child reports during separation or custody processes.
